passages.vernacularMandarin: 從前有一隻貓,他那麼警惕,老鼠們幾乎不敢露出鬍鬚尖,怕被活活吃掉。那隻貓好像同時無處不在,爪子隨時準備撲過來。最後老鼠們緊緊待在洞裡,貓看出他得好好動腦筋才能抓到一隻。於是有一天他爬上一個架子,頭朝下倒掛著,好像死了一樣,用一隻爪子抓住幾根繩子把自己吊著。

passages.original: When the Mice peeped out and saw him in that position, they thought he had been hung up there in punishment for some misdeed. Very timidly at first they stuck out their heads and sniffed about carefully. But as nothing stirred, all trooped joyfully out to celebrate the death of the Cat.
passages.vernacular: 老鼠哋探頭睇見佢嗰個姿勢,以為佢係因為做咗乜嘢壞事而被吊喺嗰度受懲罰。起初好膽怯地,佢哋伸出頭,小心地四處嗅。但因點解都冇動,所有老鼠歡天喜地地成群出嚟慶祝貓嘅死亡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老鼠們探頭看見他那個姿勢,以為他是因為做了什麼壞事而被吊在那裡受懲罰。起初非常膽怯地,他們伸出頭,小心地四處嗅。但因為什麼也沒動,所有老鼠歡天喜地地成群出來慶祝貓的死亡。

passages.original: Just then the Cat let go his hold, and before the Mice recovered from their surprise, he had made an end of three or four.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,貓鬆開咗手,老鼠哋仲冇從驚訝中恢復過嚟,佢已經解決咗三四隻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,貓鬆開了手,老鼠們還沒從驚訝中恢復過來,他已經解決了三四隻。

passages.original: Now the Mice kept more strictly at home than ever. But the Cat, who was still hungry for Mice, knew more tricks than one. Rolling himself in flour until he was covered completely, he lay down in the flour bin, with one eye open for the Mice.
passages.vernacular: 而家老鼠哋比以往任何時候都更嚴格地待喺家裡。但係貓對老鼠仍然飢餓,佢懂嘅把戲不止一個。佢喺麵粉裡打滾,直到全身都蓋滿喇,然後躺喺麵粉箱裡,一隻眼睛睜住等老鼠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在老鼠們比以往任何時候都更嚴格地待在家裡。但是貓對老鼠仍然飢餓,他懂的把戲不止一個。他在麵粉裡打滾,直到全身都蓋滿了,然後躺在麵粉箱裡,一隻眼睛睜著等老鼠。

passages.original: Sure enough, the Mice soon began to come out. To the Cat it was almost as if he already had a plump young Mouse under his claws, when an old Rat, who had had much experience with Cats and traps, and had even lost a part of his tail to pay for it, sat up at a safe distance from a hole in the wall where he lived.
passages.vernacular: 果然,老鼠哋好快開始出嚟喇。對貓來講,幾乎就像係已經有一隻肥嫩嘅小老鼠喺佢爪下喇,呢陣一隻老鼠,佢有好多對付貓同捕鼠器嘅經驗,甚至為此失去咗一截尾巴,坐喺離佢住嘅牆洞一個安全距離嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 果然,老鼠們很快開始出來了。對貓來說,幾乎就像是已經有一隻肥嫩的小老鼠在他爪下了,這時一隻老鼠,他有很多對付貓和捕鼠器的經驗,甚至為此失去了一截尾巴,坐在離他住的牆洞一個安全距離的地方。

passages.original: "Take care!" he cried. "That may be a heap of meal, but it looks to me very much like the Cat. Whatever it is, it is wisest to keep at a safe distance."
passages.vernacular: 「小心!」佢喊道。「嗰或者係一堆麵粉,可喺我睇來,佢好像貓。不管佢係乜嘢,最明智嘅係保持安全距離。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「小心!」他喊道。「那也許是一堆麵粉,可在我看來,它非常像貓。不管它是什麼,最明智的是保持安全距離。」

passages.original: The wise do not let themselves be tricked a second time.
passages.vernacular: 聰明人唔會讓自己第二次被騙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聰明人不會讓自己第二次被騙。

chapters.title: The Fox and the Crow 狐狸與烏鴉

passages.original: CH One bright morning as the Fox was following his sharp nose through the wood in search of a bite to eat, he saw a Crow on the limb of a tree overhead. This was by no means the first Crow the Fox had ever seen. What caught his attention this time and made him stop for a second look, was that the lucky Crow held a bit of cheese in her beak.
passages.vernacular: 一個晴朗嘅早晨,狐狸循住佢靈敏嘅鼻子穿過樹林尋找食嘅,佢睇見頭頂嘅樹枝上有一隻烏鴉。呢絕唔係狐狸見過嘅第一隻烏鴉。呢次吸引佢注意並讓佢停下再睇一眼嘅,係呢隻幸運嘅烏鴉嘴裡叼住一小塊乳酪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個晴朗的早晨,狐狸循著他靈敏的鼻子穿過樹林尋找吃的,他看見頭頂的樹枝上有一隻烏鴉。這絕不是狐狸見過的第一隻烏鴉。這次吸引他注意並讓他停下再看一眼的,是這隻幸運的烏鴉嘴裡叼著一小塊乳酪。

passages.original: "No need to search any farther," thought sly Master Fox. "Here is a dainty bite for my breakfast."
passages.vernacular: 「唔使再往遠處找喇,」狡猾嘅狐狸先生想。「呢度有一份美味嘅小點心當我嘅早餐。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不用再往遠處找了,」狡猾的狐狸先生想。「這裡有一份美味的小點心當我的早餐。」

passages.original: Up he trotted to the foot of the tree in which the Crow was sitting, and looking up admiringly, he cried, "Good-morning, beautiful creature!"
passages.vernacular: 佢小跑到烏鴉所在嘅樹腳下,仰望住讚歎地喊道:「早安,美麗嘅生物!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他小跑到烏鴉所在的樹腳下,仰望著讚歎地喊道:「早安,美麗的生物!」

passages.original: The Crow, her head cocked on one side, watched the Fox suspiciously. But she kept her beak tightly closed on the cheese and did not return his greeting.
passages.vernacular: 烏鴉歪住頭,懷疑地睇住狐狸。但佢把嘴緊緊閉住咬住乳酪,冇回應佢嘅問候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 烏鴉歪著頭,懷疑地看著狐狸。但她把嘴緊緊閉著咬住乳酪,沒有回應他的問候。

passages.original: "What a charming creature she is!" said the Fox. "How her feathers shine! What a beautiful form and what splendid wings! Such a wonderful Bird should have a very lovely voice, since everything else about her is so perfect. Could she sing just one song, I know I should hail her Queen of Birds."
passages.vernacular: 「佢係幾咁迷人嘅生物啊!」狐狸講。「佢嘅羽毛幾咁閃亮!多美嘅身材,幾咁華麗嘅翅膀!咁奇妙嘅鳥,應該有好可愛嘅嗓音,因為佢其他一切都咁完美。只要佢能唱一首歌,我知道我會歡呼佢為鳥中之後。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她是多麼迷人的生物啊!」狐狸說。「她的羽毛多麼閃亮!多美的身材,多麼華麗的翅膀!這麼奇妙的鳥,應該有非常可愛的嗓音,因為她其他一切都這麼完美。只要她能唱一首歌,我知道我會歡呼她為鳥中之後。」

passages.original: Listening to these flattering words, the Crow forgot all her suspicion, and also her breakfast. She wanted very much to be called Queen of Birds.
passages.vernacular: 聽住呢啲奉承嘅話,烏鴉忘咗佢所有嘅懷疑,都忘咗佢嘅早餐。佢好想被稱為鳥中之後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽著這些奉承的話,烏鴉忘了她所有的懷疑,也忘了她的早餐。她非常想被稱為鳥中之後。

passages.original: So she opened her beak wide to utter her loudest caw, and down fell the cheese straight into the Fox's open mouth.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢張大嘴巴,發出最響亮嘅呱聲,乳酪就直直掉進狐狸張住嘅嘴裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是她張大嘴巴,發出最響亮的呱聲,乳酪就直直掉進狐狸張著的嘴裡。

passages.original: "Thank you," said Master Fox sweetly, as he walked off. "Though it is cracked, you have a voice sure enough. But where are your wits?"
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝,」狐狸先生甜甜地講,走開喇。「雖然破喇,你嘅嗓子確實有。不過你嘅腦子呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝,」狐狸先生甜甜地說,走開了。「雖然破了,你的嗓子確實有。可是你的腦子呢?」

passages.original: The flatterer lives at the expense of those who will listen to him.
passages.vernacular: 奉承者靠嗰啲愛聽佢奉承嘅人為生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奉承者靠那些愛聽他奉承的人為生。

chapters.title: The Ass and Its Shadow 驢子與牠的影子

passages.original: CH A Traveler had hired an Ass to carry him to a distant part of the country. The owner of the Ass went with the Traveler, walking beside him to drive the Ass and point out the way.
passages.vernacular: 一個旅行者雇咗一頭驢子,載佢到呢個國家嘅遠處。驢子嘅主人同旅行者同行,走喺佢旁邊,趕驢並指路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個旅行者雇了一頭驢子,載他到這個國家的遠處。驢子的主人和旅行者同行,走在他旁邊,趕驢並指路。

passages.original: The road led across a treeless plain where the Sun beat down fiercely. So intense did the heat become, that the Traveler at last decided to stop for a rest, and as there was no other shade to be found, the Traveler sat down in the shadow of the Ass.
passages.vernacular: 路穿過一片冇樹嘅平原,太陽猛烈地曬住。熱得咁厲害,旅行者最後決定停下嚟休息,因為找唔到別嘅樹蔭,旅行者就坐喺驢子嘅影子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 路穿過一片沒有樹的平原,太陽猛烈地曬著。熱得那麼厲害,旅行者最後決定停下來休息,因為找不到別的樹蔭,旅行者就坐在驢子的影子裡。

passages.original: Now the heat had affected the Driver as much as it had the Traveler, and even more, for he had been walking. Wishing also to rest in the shade cast by the Ass, he began to quarrel with the Traveler, saying he had hired the Ass and not the shadow it cast.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣熱度對趕驢人嘅影響同對旅行者一樣大,甚至更大,因為佢一直喺走路。佢都想喺驢子投下嘅影子裡休息,就開始同旅行者爭吵,講佢雇嘅係驢,唔係驢投下嘅影子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時熱度對趕驢人的影響和對旅行者一樣大,甚至更大,因為他一直在走路。他也想在驢子投下的影子裡休息,就開始同旅行者爭吵,說他雇的是驢,不是驢投下的影子。

passages.original: The two soon came to blows, and while they were fighting, the Ass took to its heels.
passages.vernacular: 兩人好快動起手嚟,佢哋打架時,驢子拔腿跑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩人很快動起手來,他們打架時,驢子拔腿跑了。

passages.original: In quarreling about the shadow we often lose the substance.
passages.vernacular: 為了爭吵影子,我哋往往失去咗實質。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了爭吵影子,我們往往失去了實質。

chapters.title: The Miller, His Son, and the Ass 磨坊主、他的兒子與驢子

passages.original: CH One day, a long time ago, an old Miller and his Son were on their way to market with an Ass which they hoped to sell. They drove him very slowly, for they thought they would have a better chance to sell him if they kept him in good condition. As they walked along the highway some travelers laughed loudly at them.
passages.vernacular: 好久以前嘅一天,一個老磨坊主同佢嘅兒子,帶住一頭佢哋希望賣掉嘅驢,正往市場去。佢哋趕得好慢,因為佢哋想,把驢保持喺良好狀態,賣出去嘅機會更大。佢哋沿住大路走時,啲旅人大聲嘲笑佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很久以前的一天,一個老磨坊主和他的兒子,帶著一頭他們希望賣掉的驢,正往市場去。他們趕得很慢,因為他們想,把驢保持在良好狀態,賣出去的機會更大。他們沿著大路走時,一些旅人大聲嘲笑他們。

passages.original: "What foolishness," cried one, "to walk when they might as well ride. The most stupid of the three is not the one you would expect it to be."
passages.vernacular: 「多傻啊,」其中一個喊道,「明明可以騎,卻要走路。三個裡最蠢嘅,唔係你所想嘅嗰個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多傻啊,」其中一個喊道,「明明可以騎,卻要走路。三個裡最蠢的,不是你所想的那個。」

passages.original: The Miller did not like to be laughed at, so he told his son to climb up and ride.
passages.vernacular: 磨坊主不鍾意被嘲笑,就叫佢兒子爬上去騎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 磨坊主不喜歡被嘲笑,就叫他兒子爬上去騎。

passages.original: They had gone a little farther along the road, when three merchants passed by.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋沿路再往前走咗啲,三個商人經過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們沿路再往前走了一點,三個商人經過。

passages.original: "Oho, what have we here?" they cried. "Respect old age, young man! Get down, and let the old man ride."
passages.vernacular: 「哦嗬,呢個係點回事?」佢哋喊道。「尊敬老人,年輕人!下嚟,讓老人騎。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦嗬,這是怎麼回事?」他們喊道。「尊敬老人,年輕人!下來,讓老人騎。」

passages.original: Though the Miller was not tired, he made the boy get down and climbed up himself to ride, just to please the Merchants.
passages.vernacular: 雖然磨坊主不累,佢為了討好商人哋,定係叫男孩下嚟,自己爬上去騎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然磨坊主不累,他為了討好商人們,還是叫男孩下來,自己爬上去騎。

passages.original: At the next turnstile they overtook some women carrying market baskets loaded with vegetables and other things to sell.
passages.vernacular: 喺下一個旋轉門處,佢哋趕上咗啲婦女,佢哋攞住裝滿蔬菜同其他待售物品嘅市場籃子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在下一個旋轉門處,他們趕上了一些婦女,她們拿著裝滿蔬菜和其他待售物品的市場籃子。

passages.original: "Look at the old fool," exclaimed one of them. "Perched on the Ass, while that poor boy has to walk."
passages.vernacular: 「睇嗰老傻瓜,」其中一個喊道。「自己坐喺驢上,讓嗰個可憐嘅男孩走路。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看那老傻瓜,」其中一個喊道。「自己坐在驢上,讓那個可憐的男孩走路。」

passages.original: The Miller felt a bit vexed, but to be agreeable he told the Boy to climb up behind him.
passages.vernacular: 磨坊主有點惱火,但為了和氣,佢叫男孩爬上去坐喺佢後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 磨坊主有點惱火,但為了和氣,他叫男孩爬上去坐在他後面。

passages.original: They had no sooner started out again than a loud shout went up from another company of people on the road.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋剛又出發,路上另一群人就爆發出一陣大叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們剛又出發,路上另一群人就爆發出一陣大叫。

passages.original: "What a crime," cried one, "to load up a poor dumb beast like that! They look more able to carry the poor creature, than he to carry them."
passages.vernacular: 「幾咁過分,」一個喊道,「咁樣壓一個可憐嘅啞巴牲口!睇起嚟佢哋倆比呢可憐嘅牲口,更有能力揹牠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多麼過分,」一個喊道,「這樣壓一個可憐的啞巴牲口!看起來他們倆比這可憐的牲口,更有能力揹牠。」

passages.original: "They must be on their way to sell the poor thing's hide," said another.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋一定係要去賣呢可憐嘢嘅皮,」另一個講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們一定是要去賣這可憐東西的皮,」另一個說。

passages.original: The Miller and his Son quickly scrambled down, and a short time later, the market place was thrown into an uproar as the two came along carrying the Donkey slung from a pole. A great crowd of people ran out to get a closer look at the strange sight.
passages.vernacular: 磨坊主同佢嘅兒子趕緊爬下嚟,不久後,當兩人過嚟,用一根桿子扛住驢子時,市場裡一片騷動。一大群人跑出嚟,要近睇呢奇怪嘅景象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 磨坊主和他的兒子趕緊爬下來,不久後,當兩人過來,用一根桿子扛著驢子時,市場裡一片騷動。一大群人跑出來,要近看這奇怪的景象。

passages.original: The Ass did not dislike being carried, but so many people came up to point at him and laugh and shout, that he began to kick and bray, and then, just as they were crossing a bridge, the ropes that held him gave way, and down he tumbled into the river.
passages.vernacular: 驢子並不討厭被抬住,但咁多人過嚟指住佢笑、叫,佢開始踢同叫,然後,就喺佢哋過橋時,綁住佢嘅繩子斷喇,佢撲通掉進咗河裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 驢子並不討厭被抬著,但那麼多人過來指著他笑、叫,他開始踢和叫,然後,就在他們過橋時,綁著他的繩子斷了,他撲通掉進了河裡。

passages.original: The poor Miller now set out sadly for home. By trying to please everybody, he had pleased nobody, and lost his Ass besides.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅磨坊主而家悲傷地回家喇。佢為了取悅每個人,結果邊個都冇取悅,仲丟咗佢嘅驢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的磨坊主現在悲傷地回家了。他為了取悅每個人,結果誰也沒取悅,還丟了他的驢。

passages.original: If you try to please all, you please none.
passages.vernacular: 如果你想取悅所有人,你就邊個都取悅不喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你想取悅所有人,你就誰也取悅不了。

chapters.title: The Ant and the Dove 螞蟻與鴿子

passages.original: CH A Dove saw an Ant fall into a brook. The Ant struggled in vain to reach the bank, and in pity, the Dove dropped a blade of straw close beside it. Clinging to the straw like a shipwrecked sailor to a broken spar, the Ant floated safely to shore.
passages.vernacular: 一隻鴿子睇見一隻螞蟻掉進小溪。螞蟻徒勞地掙扎著想到岸邊,出於憐憫,鴿子喺佢旁邊放下一根草稈。螞蟻像遇難嘅水手抓住斷裂嘅桅桿一樣抓住草稈,安全漂到咗岸上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻鴿子看見一隻螞蟻掉進小溪。螞蟻徒勞地掙扎著想到岸邊,出於憐憫,鴿子在它旁邊放下一根草稈。螞蟻像遇難的水手抓住斷裂的桅桿一樣抓著草稈,安全漂到了岸上。

passages.original: Soon after, the Ant saw a man getting ready to kill the Dove with a stone. But just as he cast the stone, the Ant stung him in the heel, so that the pain made him miss his aim, and the startled Dove flew to safety in a distant wood.
passages.vernacular: 不久之後,螞蟻睇見一個人正準備用石頭打死鴿子。但就喺佢扔出石頭時,螞蟻蜇咗佢嘅腳後跟,疼痛使佢射偏喇,受驚嘅鴿子飛到遠處樹林裡安全喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久之後,螞蟻看見一個人正準備用石頭打死鴿子。但就在他扔出石頭時,螞蟻蜇了他的腳後跟,疼痛使他射偏了,受驚的鴿子飛到遠處樹林裡安全了。

passages.original: A kindness is never wasted.
passages.vernacular: 善意永遠唔會白費。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 善意永遠不會白費。

chapters.title: The Man and the Satyr 人與薩提爾

passages.original: CH A long time ago a Man met a Satyr in the forest and succeeded in making friends with him. The two soon became the best of comrades, living together in the Man's hut. But one cold winter evening, as they were walking homeward, the Satyr saw the Man blow on his fingers.
passages.vernacular: 好久以前,一個人喺森林裡遇到一個薩提爾,並成功地同佢交上咗朋友。兩人好快成咗最好嘅夥伴,一起住喺嗰人嘅小屋裡。但係一個寒冷嘅冬夜,佢哋走路回家時,薩提爾睇見嗰人對住佢嘅手指吹氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很久以前,一個人在森林裡遇到一個薩提爾,並成功地同他交上了朋友。兩人很快成了最好的夥伴,一起住在那人的小屋裡。但是一個寒冷的冬夜,他們走路回家時,薩提爾看見那人對著他的手指吹氣。

passages.original: "Why do you do that?" asked the Satyr.
passages.vernacular: 「你點解嗰樣做?」薩提爾問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼那樣做?」薩提爾問。

passages.original: "To warm my hands," the Man replied.
passages.vernacular: 「為了暖手,」嗰人回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為了暖手,」那人回答。

passages.original: When they reached home the Man prepared two bowls of porridge. These he placed steaming hot on the table, and the comrades sat down very cheerfully to enjoy the meal. But much to the Satyr's surprise, the Man began to blow into his bowl of porridge.
passages.vernacular: 到家後,嗰人準備咗兩碗粥。佢把佢哋熱氣騰騰地放喺桌上,夥伴哋好愉快地坐下嚟享用呢頓飯。但令薩提爾大為驚訝嘅係,嗰人開始對住佢嗰碗粥吹氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到家後,那人準備了兩碗粥。他把它們熱氣騰騰地放在桌上,夥伴們很愉快地坐下來享用這頓飯。但令薩提爾大為驚訝的是,那人開始對著他那碗粥吹氣。

passages.original: "Why do you do that?" he asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你點解嗰樣做?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼那樣做?」他問。

passages.original: "To cool my porridge," replied the Man.
passages.vernacular: 「為了讓我嘅粥涼,」嗰人回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為了讓我的粥涼,」那人回答。

passages.original: The Satyr sprang hurriedly to his feet and made for the door.
passages.vernacular: 薩提爾匆忙跳起嚟,朝門走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 薩提爾匆忙跳起來,朝門走去。

passages.original: "Goodby," he said, "I've seen enough. A fellow that blows hot and cold in the same breath cannot be friends with me!"
passages.vernacular: 「再見,」佢講,「我睇夠喇。一個同一口氣又吹熱又吹冷嘅傢伙,唔能夠同我做朋友!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再見,」他說,「我看夠了。一個同一口氣又吹熱又吹冷的傢伙,不能同我做朋友!」

passages.original: The man who talks for both sides is not to be trusted by either.
passages.vernacular: 兩邊都講話嘅人,任何一邊都唔能夠信任佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩邊都說話的人,任何一邊都不能信任他。

chapters.title: The Wolf, the Kid, and the Goat 狼、小山羊與山羊媽媽

passages.original: CH Mother Goat was going to market one morning to get provisions for her household, which consisted of but one little Kid and herself.
passages.vernacular: 山羊媽媽一天早晨要去市場為佢嘅家買嘢,佢嘅家只有一隻小山羊同佢自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 山羊媽媽一天早晨要去市場為她的家買東西,她的家只有一隻小山羊和她自己。

passages.original: "Take good care of the house, my son," she said to the Kid, as she carefully latched the door. "Do not let anyone in, unless he gives you this password: 'Down with the Wolf and all his race!'"
passages.vernacular: 「好好睇家,我嘅細路,」佢對小山羊講,小心地閂上咗門。「除非有人講出呢個暗號,否則唔好讓任何人進嚟:『打倒狼同佢所有嘅同類!』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好好看家,我的孩子,」她對小山羊說,小心地閂上了門。「除非有人說出這個暗號,否則不要讓任何人進來:『打倒狼和他所有的同類!』」

passages.original: Strangely enough, a Wolf was lurking near and heard what the Goat had said. So, as soon as Mother Goat was out of sight, up he trotted to the door and knocked.
passages.vernacular: 講來奇怪,一隻狼正潛伏喺附近,聽到咗山羊講嘅話。所以山羊媽媽一走遠,佢就小跑到門口敲門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說來奇怪,一隻狼正潛伏在附近,聽到了山羊說的話。所以山羊媽媽一走遠,他就小跑到門口敲門。

passages.original: "Down with the Wolf and all his race," said the Wolf softly.
passages.vernacular: 「打倒狼同佢所有嘅同類,」狼輕聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「打倒狼和他所有的同類,」狼輕聲說。

passages.original: It was the right password, but when the Kid peeped through a crack in the door and saw the shadowy figure outside, he did not feel at all easy.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係正確嘅暗號,不過小山羊從門縫裡窺見外面陰影般嘅身影時,佢啲都不放心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是正確的暗號,可是小山羊從門縫裡窺見外面陰影般的身影時,他一點也不放心。

passages.original: "Show me a white paw," he said, "or I won't let you in."
passages.vernacular: 「畀我睇一隻白爪子,」佢講,「否則我不讓你進嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「給我看一隻白爪子,」他說,「否則我不讓你進來。」

passages.original: A white paw, of course, is a feature few Wolves can show, and so Master Wolf had to go away as hungry as he had come.
passages.vernacular: 白爪子當然係好少有狼能展示嘅特徵,於是狼先生只好像嚟時一樣飢餓地走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 白爪子當然是很少有狼能展示的特徵,於是狼先生只好像來時一樣飢餓地走了。

passages.original: "You can never be too sure," said the Kid, when he saw the Wolf making off to the woods.
passages.vernacular: 「你永遠唔會太保險,」小山羊睇見狼往樹林裡走去時講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你永遠不會太保險,」小山羊看見狼往樹林裡走去時說。

passages.original: Two sureties are better than one.
passages.vernacular: 兩重保險勝過一重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩重保險勝過一重。

chapters.title: The Swallow and the Crow 燕子與烏鴉

passages.original: CH The Swallow and the Crow had an argument one day about their plumage.
passages.vernacular: 有一天,燕子同烏鴉為牠哋嘅羽毛爭論起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天,燕子和烏鴉為牠們的羽毛爭論起來。

passages.original: Said the Swallow: "Just look at my bright and downy feathers. Your black stiff quills are not worth having. Why don't you dress better? Show a little pride!"
passages.vernacular: 燕子講:「睇睇我明亮柔軟嘅羽毛。你嗰黑色僵硬嘅羽管不值得擁有。你點解不穿得好啲?顯示啲驕傲吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 燕子說:「看看我明亮柔軟的羽毛。你那黑色僵硬的羽管不值得擁有。你為什麼不穿得好一點?顯示一點驕傲吧!」

passages.original: "Your feathers may do very well in spring," replied the Crow, "but--I don't remember ever having seen you around in winter, and that's when I enjoy myself most."
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅羽毛喺春天或者好好,」烏鴉回答,「但係——我不記得冬天曾喺附近見過你,而嗰正是我最享受嘅時候。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的羽毛在春天也許很好,」烏鴉回答,「但是——我不記得冬天曾在附近見過你,而那正是我最享受的時候。」

passages.original: Friends in fine weather only, are not worth much.
passages.vernacular: 只喺好天氣裡交往嘅朋友,冇多大價值。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只在好天氣裡交往的朋友,沒有多大價值。

chapters.title: Jupiter and the Monkey 朱比特與猴子

passages.original: CH There was once a baby show among the Animals in the forest. Jupiter provided the prize. Of course all the proud mammas from far and near brought their babies. But none got there earlier than Mother Monkey. Proudly she presented her baby among the other contestants.
passages.vernacular: 森林裡嘅動物哋曾經舉辦過一場嬰兒選美。朱比特提供獎品。當然,遠近所有驕傲嘅媽媽哋都把佢哋嘅寶寶帶嚟喇。但冇邊個比猴媽媽到得更早。佢驕傲地喺其他參賽者中展示佢嘅寶寶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 森林裡的動物們曾經舉辦過一場嬰兒選美。朱比特提供獎品。當然,遠近所有驕傲的媽媽們都把她們的寶寶帶來了。但沒有誰比猴媽媽到得更早。她驕傲地在其他參賽者中展示她的寶寶。

passages.original: As you can imagine, there was quite a laugh when the Animals saw the ugly flat-nosed, hairless, pop-eyed little creature.
passages.vernacular: 你可以想像,動物哋睇到嗰隻醜陋嘅塌鼻子、冇毛、凸眼睛嘅小生物時,係點樣一陣哄笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以想像,動物們看到那隻醜陋的塌鼻子、沒有毛、凸眼睛的小生物時,是怎樣一陣哄笑。

passages.original: "Laugh if you will," said the Mother Monkey. "Though Jupiter may not give him the prize, I know that he is the prettiest, the sweetest, the dearest darling in the world."
passages.vernacular: 「你哋想笑就笑吧,」猴媽媽講。「雖然朱比特或者唔會把獎品畀佢,我知道佢係世上最漂亮、最可愛、最親愛嘅心肝寶貝。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們想笑就笑吧,」猴媽媽說。「雖然朱比特也許不會把獎品給他,我知道他是世上最漂亮、最可愛、最親愛的心肝寶貝。」

passages.original: Mother love is blind.
passages.vernacular: 母愛係盲目的。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 母愛是盲目的。

chapters.title: The Lion, the Ass, and the Fox 獅子、驢子與狐狸

passages.original: CH A Lion, an Ass, and a Fox were hunting in company, and caught a large quantity of game. The Ass was asked to divide the spoil. This he did very fairly, giving each an equal share.
passages.vernacular: 一頭獅子、一頭驢子同一隻狐狸結伴打獵,捕獲咗大量獵物。驢子被請去分配戰利品。佢分得好公平,每人得到相等嘅一份。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一頭獅子、一頭驢子和一隻狐狸結伴打獵,捕獲了大量獵物。驢子被請去分配戰利品。他分得很公平,每人得到相等的一份。

passages.original: The Fox was well satisfied, but the Lion flew into a great rage over it, and with one stroke of his huge paw, he added the Ass to the pile of slain.
passages.vernacular: 狐狸好滿意,不過獅子對此大發雷霆,用佢巨大嘅爪子一擊,把驢子都加到被殺者嘅堆裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狐狸很滿意,可是獅子對此大發雷霆,用他巨大的爪子一擊,把驢子也加到被殺者的堆裡。

passages.original: Then he turned to the Fox.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢轉向狐狸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他轉向狐狸。

passages.original: "You divide it," he roared angrily.
passages.vernacular: 「你嚟分,」佢憤怒地吼道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你來分,」他憤怒地吼道。

passages.original: The Fox wasted no time in talking. He quickly piled all the game into one great heap. From this he took a very small portion for himself, such undesirable bits as the horns and hoofs of a mountain goat, and the end of an ox tail.
passages.vernacular: 狐狸不浪費時間講話。佢迅速把所有獵物堆成一大堆。從中佢畀自己只攞咗好小一部分,係嗰啲唔想要嘅零碎,比如一隻野山羊嘅角同蹄子,以及一截牛尾巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狐狸不浪費時間說話。他迅速把所有獵物堆成一大堆。從中他給自己只拿了很小一部分,是那些不想要的零碎,比如一隻野山羊的角和蹄子,以及一截牛尾巴。

passages.original: The Lion now recovered his good humor entirely.
passages.vernacular: 獅子而家完全恢復咗好心情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子現在完全恢復了好心情。

passages.original: "Who taught you to divide so fairly?" he asked pleasantly.
passages.vernacular: 「邊個教你分得咁公平嘅?」佢愉快地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「誰教你分得這麼公平的?」他愉快地問。

passages.original: "I learned a lesson from the Ass," replied the Fox, carefully edging away.
passages.vernacular: 「我從驢子嗰度學咗一課,」狐狸回答,小心地往旁邊挪開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從驢子那裡學了一課,」狐狸回答,小心地往旁邊挪開。

passages.original: Learn from the misfortunes of others.
passages.vernacular: 從別人嘅不幸中學習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從別人的不幸中學習。

chapters.title: The Lion's Share 獅子的一份

passages.original: CH A long time ago, the Lion, the Fox, the Jackal, and the Wolf agreed to go hunting together, sharing with each other whatever they found.
passages.vernacular: 好久以前,獅子、狐狸、豺同狼約好一起去打獵,無論找到乜嘢都互相分享。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很久以前,獅子、狐狸、豺和狼約好一起去打獵,無論找到什麼都互相分享。

passages.original: One day the Wolf ran down a Stag and immediately called his comrades to divide the spoil.
passages.vernacular: 有一天,狼追倒咗一頭雄鹿,即刻叫佢嘅夥伴哋嚟分戰利品。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天,狼追倒了一頭雄鹿,立刻叫他的夥伴們來分戰利品。

passages.original: Without being asked, the Lion placed himself at the head of the feast to do the carving, and, with a great show of fairness, began to count the guests.
passages.vernacular: 獅子冇人請就把自己放喺宴席首位去切分,並且極力表現出公平,開始數客人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子沒人請就把自己放在宴席首位去切分,並且極力表現出公平,開始數客人。

passages.original: "One," he said, counting on his claws, "that is myself the Lion. Two, that's the Wolf, three, is the Jackal, and the Fox makes four."
passages.vernacular: 「一,」佢用爪子數住講,「嗰個係我自己,獅子。二,嗰個係狼,三係豺,狐狸係四。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一,」他用爪子數著說,「那是我自己,獅子。二,那是狼,三是豺,狐狸是四。」

passages.original: He then very carefully divided the Stag into four equal parts.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢好仔細地把雄鹿分成相等嘅四份。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他非常仔細地把雄鹿分成相等的四份。

passages.original: "I am King Lion," he said, when he had finished, "so of course I get the first part. This next part falls to me because I am the strongest; and this is mine because I am the bravest."
passages.vernacular: 「我係獅子王,」佢分完後講,「所以我當然攞第一份。下一份歸我,因為我最強壯;呢一份係我嘅,因為我最勇敢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是獅子王,」他分完後說,「所以我當然拿第一份。下一份歸我,因為我最強壯;這一份是我的,因為我最勇敢。」

passages.original: He now began to glare at the others very savagely. "If any of you have any claim to the part that is left," he growled, stretching his claws meaningly, "now is the time to speak up."
passages.vernacular: 而家佢開始凶狠地瞪住其他人。「你哋中如果有邊個對剩下嘅嗰份有乜嘢要求,」佢咆哮道,意味深長地伸出爪子,「而家係講話嘅時候。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他開始凶狠地瞪著其他人。「你們中如果有誰對剩下的那份有什麼要求,」他咆哮道,意味深長地伸出爪子,「現在是說話的時候。」

passages.original: Might makes right.
passages.vernacular: 強權就係公理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 強權就是公理。

chapters.title: The Mole and His Mother 鼴鼠與他的媽媽

passages.original: CH A little Mole once said to his Mother:
passages.vernacular: 一隻小鼴鼠曾對佢母親講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻小鼴鼠曾對他母親說:

passages.original: "Why, Mother, you said I was blind! But I am sure I can see!"
passages.vernacular: 「媽媽,你講我係瞎嘅!不過我肯定我能睇見!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「媽媽,你說我是瞎的!可是我肯定我能看見!」

passages.original: Mother Mole saw she would have to get such conceit out of his head. So she put a bit of frankincense before him and asked him to tell what it was.
passages.vernacular: 鼠媽媽睇出佢必須把呢種自負從佢腦子裡弄走。於是佢喺佢面前放咗啲乳香,叫佢講嗰個係乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鼠媽媽看出她必須把這種自負從他腦子裡弄走。於是她在他面前放了一點乳香,叫他說那是什麼。

passages.original: The little Mole peered at it.
passages.vernacular: 小鼴鼠仔細睇咗睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小鼴鼠仔細看了看。

passages.original: "Why, that's a pebble!"
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,嗰個係一顆小石子!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,那是一顆小石子!」

passages.original: "Well, my son, that proves you've lost your sense of smell as well as being blind."
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,我嘅兒子,呢證明你不僅係瞎嘅,仲喪失咗嗅覺。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,我的兒子,這證明你不僅是瞎的,還喪失了嗅覺。」

passages.original: Boast of one thing and you will be found lacking in that and a few other things as well.
passages.vernacular: 吹噓一件事,你會發現你喺嗰件事同另外幾件事上都有欠缺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吹噓一件事,你會發現你在那件事和另外幾件事上都有欠缺。

chapters.title: The North Wind and the Sun 北風與太陽

passages.original: CH The North Wind and the Sun had a quarrel about which of them was the stronger. While they were disputing with much heat and bluster, a Traveler passed along the road wrapped in a cloak.
passages.vernacular: 北風同太陽爭論佢哋邊個更強。佢哋正熱烈而喧嚷地爭論時,一個旅人裹住斗篷從路上走過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 北風和太陽爭論他們誰更強。他們正熱烈而喧嚷地爭論時,一個旅人裹著斗篷從路上走過。

passages.original: "Let us agree," said the Sun, "that he is the stronger who can strip that Traveler of his cloak."
passages.vernacular: 「我哋嚟約定,」太陽講,「邊個能把嗰個旅人嘅斗篷脫下嚟,邊個就更強。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們來約定,」太陽說,「誰能把那個旅人的斗篷脫下來,誰就更強。」

passages.original: "Very well," growled the North Wind, and at once sent a cold, howling blast against the Traveler.
passages.vernacular: 「好好,」北風咆哮道,即刻對旅人吹去一陣冰冷呼嘯嘅狂風。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好,」北風咆哮道,立刻對旅人吹去一陣冰冷呼嘯的狂風。

passages.original: With the first gust of wind the ends of the cloak whipped about the Traveler's body. But he immediately wrapped it closely around him, and the harder the Wind blew, the tighter he held it to him. The North Wind tore angrily at the cloak, but all his efforts were in vain.
passages.vernacular: 第一陣風,斗篷嘅邊角就喺旅人身上亂甩。但佢即刻把佢緊緊裹喺身上,風吹得越猛,佢把佢抓得越緊。北風憤怒地撕扯斗篷,但佢所有嘅努力都係徒勞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第一陣風,斗篷的邊角就在旅人身上亂甩。但他立刻把它緊緊裹在身上,風吹得越猛,他把它抓得越緊。北風憤怒地撕扯斗篷,但他所有的努力都是徒勞。

passages.original: Then the Sun began to shine. At first his beams were gentle, and in the pleasant warmth after the bitter cold of the North Wind, the Traveler unfastened his cloak and let it hang loosely from his shoulders. The Sun's rays grew warmer and warmer. The man took off his cap and mopped his brow. At last he became so heated that he pulled off his cloak, and, to escape the blazing sunshine, threw himself down in the welcome shade of a tree by the roadside.
passages.vernacular: 然後太陽開始發光。起初佢嘅光線好溫和,喺北風嘅刺骨寒冷之後,呢愉快嘅溫暖中,旅人解開咗斗篷,讓佢鬆鬆地從肩上垂下嚟。太陽嘅光線越嚟越暖。嗰人脫下帽子,擦住額頭。最後佢熱得咁厲害,脫掉咗斗篷,為了躲避灼熱嘅陽光,佢撲倒喺路邊一棵樹嘅受歡迎嘅樹蔭下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後太陽開始發光。起初他的光線很溫和,在北風的刺骨寒冷之後,這愉快的溫暖中,旅人解開了斗篷,讓它鬆鬆地從肩上垂下來。太陽的光線越來越暖。那人脫下帽子,擦著額頭。最後他熱得那麼厲害,脫掉了斗篷,為了躲避灼熱的陽光,他撲倒在路邊一棵樹的受歡迎的樹蔭下。

passages.original: Gentleness and kind persuasion win where force and bluster fail.
passages.vernacular: 溫和同善意嘅勸講,喺武力同咆哮失敗嘅地方取勝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫和與善意的勸說,在武力與咆哮失敗的地方取勝。

chapters.title: The Hare and His Ears 兔子與牠的耳朵

passages.original: CH The Lion had been badly hurt by the horns of a Goat, which he was eating. He was very angry to think that any animal that he chose for a meal, should be so brazen as to wear such dangerous things as horns to scratch him while he ate. So he commanded that all animals with horns should leave his domains within twenty-four hours.
passages.vernacular: 獅子被一隻山羊嘅角嚴重刺傷喇,佢正在食呢隻山羊。佢好生氣,想到佢選嚟當一餐嘅任何動物,竟然厚臉皮到戴住角咁樣危險嘅嘢,喺佢食嘅時候嚟刺佢。於是佢命令所有長角嘅動物喺二十四小時內離開佢嘅領地。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獅子被一隻山羊的角嚴重刺傷了,他正在吃這隻山羊。他很生氣,想到他選來當一餐的任何動物,竟然厚臉皮到戴著角這樣危險的東西,在他吃的時候來刺他。於是他命令所有長角的動物在二十四小時內離開他的領地。

passages.original: The command struck terror among the beasts. All those who were so unfortunate as to have horns, began to pack up and move out. Even the Hare, who, as you know, has no horns and so had nothing to fear, passed a very restless night, dreaming awful dreams about the fearful Lion.
passages.vernacular: 呢道命令喺野獸中引起咗恐慌。所有嗰啲不幸長角嘅,開始收拾行李搬出去。連野兔,你知道,係冇角嘅,本來冇乜嘢可怕嘅,都度過咗一個不安嘅夜晚,夢到關於可怕獅子嘅駭人嘅夢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這道命令在野獸中引起了恐慌。所有那些不幸長角的,開始收拾行李搬出去。連野兔,你知道,是沒有角的,本來沒什麼可怕的,也度過了一個不安的夜晚,夢到關於可怕獅子的駭人的夢。

passages.original: And when he came out of the warren in the early morning sunshine, and there saw the shadow cast by his long and pointed ears, a terrible fright seized him.
passages.vernacular: 清晨佢喺陽光下從兔窩出嚟,喺嗰度睇見佢又長又尖嘅耳朵投下嘅影子,一陣可怕嘅恐懼抓住咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 清晨他在陽光下從兔窩出來,在那裡看見他又長又尖的耳朵投下的影子,一陣可怕的恐懼抓住了他。

passages.original: "Goodby, neighbor Cricket," he called. "I'm off. He will certainly make out that my ears are horns, no matter what I say."
passages.vernacular: 「再見,蟋蟀鄰居,」佢喊道。「我走喇。不管我講乜嘢,佢肯定會斷定我嘅耳朵係角。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再見,蟋蟀鄰居,」他喊道。「我走了。不管我說什麼,他肯定會斷定我的耳朵是角。」

passages.original: Do not give your enemies the slightest reason to attack your reputation.
passages.vernacular: 唔好畀你嘅敵人絲毫攻擊你名聲嘅理由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要給你的敵人絲毫攻擊你名聲的理由。

passages.original: Your enemies will seize any excuse to attack you.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅敵人會抓住任何藉口攻擊你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的敵人會抓住任何藉口攻擊你。

chapters.title: The Wolves and the Sheep 狼與羊群

passages.original: CH A pack of Wolves lurked near the Sheep pasture. But the Dogs kept them all at a respectful distance, and the Sheep grazed in perfect safety. But now the Wolves thought of a plan to trick the Sheep.
passages.vernacular: 一群狼潛伏喺羊群牧場附近。但係狗讓牠哋全都保持住恭敬嘅距離,羊群喺完全安全中食草。可而家狼想出一個計劃嚟欺騙羊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一群狼潛伏在羊群牧場附近。但是狗讓牠們全都保持著恭敬的距離,羊群在完全安全中吃草。可現在狼想出一個計劃來欺騙羊。

passages.original: "Why is there always this hostility between us?" they said. "If it were not for those Dogs who are always stirring up trouble, I am sure we should get along beautifully. Send them away and you will see what good friends we shall become."
passages.vernacular: 「點解我哋之間總是有呢種敵意?」牠哋講。「要唔係嗰啲總是挑起麻煩嘅狗,我肯定我哋會相處得好好。把牠哋趕走,你就會睇到我哋將成為幾咁好嘅朋友。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼我們之間總是有這種敵意?」牠們說。「要不是那些總是挑起麻煩的狗,我肯定我們會相處得很好。把牠們趕走,你就會看到我們將成為多麼好的朋友。」

passages.original: The Sheep were easily fooled. They persuaded the Dogs to go away, and that very evening the Wolves had the grandest feast of their lives.
passages.vernacular: 羊好容易被騙。佢哋講服咗狗離開,就喺嗰天晚上,狼過上咗一生中最盛大嘅宴會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羊很容易被騙。他們說服了狗離開,就在那天晚上,狼過上了一生中最盛大的宴會。

passages.original: Do not give up friends for foes.
passages.vernacular: 唔好為了敵人放棄朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要為了敵人放棄朋友。

chapters.title: The Cock and the Fox 公雞與狐狸(二)

passages.original: CH A Fox was caught in a trap one fine morning, because he had got too near the Farmer's hen house. No doubt he was hungry, but that was not an excuse for stealing. A Cock, rising early, discovered what had happened. He knew the Fox could not get at him, so he went a little closer to get a good look at his enemy.
passages.vernacular: 一個晴朗嘅早晨,一隻狐狸被夾喺陷阱裡,因為佢靠農夫嘅雞舍太近喇。毫無疑問佢餓喇,但嗰唔係偷竊嘅藉口。一隻公雞起得早,發現咗發生嘅事。佢知道狐狸夠唔到佢,於是走近啲,好好睇睇佢嘅敵人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個晴朗的早晨,一隻狐狸被夾在陷阱裡,因為他靠農夫的雞舍太近了。毫無疑問他餓了,但那不是偷竊的藉口。一隻公雞起得早,發現了發生的事。他知道狐狸夠不到他,於是走近一點,好好看看他的敵人。

passages.original: The Fox saw a slender chance of escape.
passages.vernacular: 狐狸睇到一線逃脫嘅機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狐狸看到一線逃脫的機會。

passages.original: "Dear friend," he said, "I was just on my way to visit a sick relative, when I stumbled into this string and got all tangled up. But please do not tell anybody about it. I dislike causing sorrow to anybody, and I am sure I can soon gnaw this string to pieces."
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅朋友,」佢講,「我正在去探望一個生病嘅親戚嘅路上,絆到咗呢根繩子,纏成咗一團。但請唔好告訴任何人。我不鍾意讓任何人傷心,我肯定我好快就能把呢根繩子咬成碎片。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的朋友,」他說,「我正在去探望一個生病的親戚的路上,絆到了這根繩子,纏成了一團。但請不要告訴任何人。我不喜歡讓任何人傷心,我肯定我很快就能把這根繩子咬成碎片。」

passages.original: But the Cock was not to be so easily fooled. He soon roused the whole hen yard, and when the Farmer came running out, that was the end of Mr. Fox.
passages.vernacular: 但公雞唔係咁容易被騙嘅。佢好快喚醒咗整個雞院,農夫跑出嚟時,狐狸先生就完蛋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但公雞不是那麼容易被騙的。他很快喚醒了整個雞院,農夫跑出來時,狐狸先生就完蛋了。

passages.original: The wicked deserve no aid.
passages.vernacular: 邪惡嘅人不值得幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 邪惡的人不值得幫助。

chapters.title: The Ass in the Lion's Skin 披著獅子皮的驢子

passages.original: CH An Ass found a Lion's skin left in the forest by a hunter. He dressed himself in it, and amused himself by hiding in a thicket and rushing out suddenly at the animals who passed that way. All took to their heels the moment they saw him.
passages.vernacular: 一頭驢子發現咗一張獅子皮,係獵人留喺森林裡嘅。佢把佢穿上,躲喺灌木叢裡,突然衝出嚟嚇經過嗰度嘅動物,以此取樂。所有動物一睇見佢就拔腿逃跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一頭驢子發現了一張獅子皮,是獵人留在森林裡的。他把它穿上,躲在灌木叢裡,突然衝出來嚇經過那裡的動物,以此取樂。所有動物一看見他就拔腿逃跑。

passages.original: The Ass was so pleased to see the animals running away from him, just as if he were King Lion himself, that he could not keep from expressing his delight by a loud, harsh bray. A Fox, who ran with the rest, stopped short as soon as he heard the voice. Approaching the Ass, he said with a laugh:
passages.vernacular: 驢子睇到動物哋從佢面前逃跑,就好像佢係獅子國王本人一樣,好高興,忍不住發出一聲響亮刺耳嘅驢叫嚟表達佢嘅喜悅。一隻同其他動物一起跑嘅狐狸,一聽到嗰聲音就突然停住。佢走近驢子,笑住講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 驢子看到動物們從他面前逃跑,就好像他是獅子國王本人一樣,非常高興,忍不住發出一聲響亮刺耳的驢叫來表達他的喜悅。一隻同其他動物一起跑的狐狸,一聽到那聲音就突然停住。他走近驢子,笑著說:

passages.original: "If you had kept your mouth shut you might have frightened me, too. But you gave yourself away with that silly bray."
passages.vernacular: 「如果你閉住嘴,你或者連我都嚇到喇。但你用嗰愚蠢嘅驢叫暴露咗你自己。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你閉著嘴,你也許連我也嚇到了。但你用那愚蠢的驢叫暴露了你自己。」

passages.original: A fool may deceive by his dress and appearance, but his words will soon show what he really is.
passages.vernacular: 傻瓜可以靠佢嘅衣住同外表騙人,但佢嘅話好快就會顯示佢到底係乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傻瓜可以靠他的衣著和外表騙人,但他的話很快就會顯示他到底是什麼。

chapters.title: The Fisherman and the Little Fish 漁夫與小魚

passages.original: CH A poor Fisherman, who lived on the fish he caught, had bad luck one day and caught nothing but a very small fry. The Fisherman was about to put it in his basket when the little Fish said:
passages.vernacular: 一個窮漁夫靠捕到嘅魚為生,有一天運氣不好,只捕到一條好小嘅魚苗。漁夫正要把佢放進籃子時,小魚講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個窮漁夫靠捕到的魚為生,有一天運氣不好,只捕到一條很小的魚苗。漁夫正要把它放進籃子時,小魚說:

passages.original: "Please spare me, Mr. Fisherman! I am so small it is not worth while to carry me home. When I am bigger, I shall make you a much better meal."
passages.vernacular: 「請放過我吧,漁夫先生!我咁小,把我帶回家不值得。等我長大喇,我會成為你一頓好得多嘅飯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請放過我吧,漁夫先生!我這麼小,把我帶回家不值得。等我長大了,我會成為你一頓好得多的飯。」

passages.original: But the Fisherman quickly put the fish into his basket.
passages.vernacular: 但漁夫好快把魚放進咗籃子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但漁夫很快把魚放進了籃子。

passages.original: "How foolish I should be," he said, "to throw you back. However small you may be, you are better than nothing at all."
passages.vernacular: 「我扔回你去,嗰得多傻啊,」佢講。「不管你多小,總比乜嘢都冇好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我扔回你去,那得多傻啊,」他說。「不管你多小,總比什麼也沒有好。」

passages.original: A small gain is worth more than a large promise.
passages.vernacular: 小小嘅收穫勝過大大嘅承諾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小小的收穫勝過大大的承諾。

chapters.title: The Fighting Cocks and the Eagle 打架的公雞與老鷹

passages.original: CH Once there were two Cocks living in the same farmyard who could not bear the sight of each other. At last one day they flew up to fight it out, beak and claw. They fought until one of them was beaten and crawled off to a corner to hide.
passages.vernacular: 從前有兩隻公雞住喺同一個農場裡,彼此邊個都睇不順眼。終於有一天,佢哋飛起嚟用嘴同爪子決一死戰。佢哋打啊打,直到其中一隻被打敗,爬到一個角落裡躲起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從前有兩隻公雞住在同一個農場裡,彼此誰也看不順眼。終於有一天,他們飛起來用嘴和爪子決一死戰。他們打啊打,直到其中一隻被打敗,爬到一個角落裡躲起來。

passages.original: The Cock that had won the battle flew to the top of the hen-house, and, proudly flapping his wings, crowed with all his might to tell the world about his victory. But an Eagle, circling overhead, heard the boasting chanticleer and, swooping down, carried him off to his nest.
passages.vernacular: 贏得咗戰鬥嘅公雞飛到雞舍頂上,驕傲地拍住翅膀,拚命啼叫,把佢嘅勝利告訴世界。但係一隻喺頭頂盤旋嘅老鷹,聽到咗吹噓嘅公雞,俯衝下嚟,把佢帶回咗巢裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 贏得了戰鬥的公雞飛到雞舍頂上,驕傲地拍著翅膀,拚命啼叫,把他的勝利告訴世界。但是一隻在頭頂盤旋的老鷹,聽到了吹噓的公雞,俯衝下來,把他帶回了巢裡。

passages.original: His rival saw the deed, and coming out of his corner, took his place as master of the farmyard.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅對手睇到咗呢一幕,從角落裡出嚟,取代咗佢,成為農場嘅主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的對手看到了這一幕,從角落裡出來,取代了他,成為農場的主人。

passages.original: Pride goes before a fall.
passages.vernacular: 驕傲喺跌倒之前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 驕傲在跌倒之前。
